sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a decelerating ramp: growth ran 104.0% in FY2017 and 64.2% in FY2021, then fell to 0.1% in FY2023 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D36][D218][D311][D406].
FY2017's operating loss of $3,485.6 million was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the IPO-related RSUs and the CEO award [F12][P74].
The FY2022 reversal, with the operating loss widening 98.7% to $1,395.3 million, came from higher cost of revenue and operating expenses against only 11.8% revenue growth [F17][D264][D263][P42].
Since FY2023 the loss has narrowed every year, from -30.4% of revenue to -9.0% in FY2025, the best margin in the window [F28][F30][D554].
North America still supplied the largest slice of FY2025 growth at +4.4pp of the 10.6% total, but its share of revenue fell to 58.6% from 81.9% in FY2017 [D458][D406][D456][D434].
Rest of world contributed +3.7pp on 17.0% growth and now is 23.0% of revenue, while Europe added +2.5pp [D499][D498][D497][D524].
Advertising revenue rose 5.8% to $5,186.1 million on roughly 17% more impressions, offset by a 10% lower cost per impression [S39][D537][P24].
Other revenue grew 62.9% to $745.4 million, now 12.6% of the total, on higher subscription revenue from subscriber growth [S42][D544][D543][P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth, so the incremental operating margin was 44.8% [D423][D406][D429].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is far above the -32.4% window median and the -422.5% low, but still 29.3pp below the 20.3% internet peer median [F30][D555][D553][D571].
Cost of revenue eased 1.1pp to 45.0% of revenue and R&D 1.3pp to 30.2%, while other lines added 3.3pp, lifting the margin 5.7pp [D386][D431][D387][D432][D433][D419].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events and lower advertising, partly offset by higher headcount [X50][P22].
R&D rose $101.9 million on product development and headcount, and G&A rose $60.0 million on external professional services including legal [X40][P23][X60][P21].
Net margin of -7.8% beat operating margin by 1.2pp, helped by $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains in other income [F50][F30][P18].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million and free cash flow of $437.2 million both exceeded the $460.5 million net loss in FY2025, a 7.4% free-cash-flow margin [F80][F100][F40][D393].
The gap is non-cash: stock-based compensation of $1.0 billion and D&A of $163.6 million were added back to the net loss [P13][X90][X80].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A, up from 3.6% and 1.23x in FY2024 [F90][D392][D395][D344][D347].
Capex is mainly improvements to leased facilities to support team workspaces, not capacity expansion [P10].
Net cash swung from $1,439.8 million in FY2021 to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, -10.1% of revenue versus a 45.0% peer median [D211][D399][D400][D579].
Debt rose to $3,536.8 million as $1.4 billion of notes were repurchased and $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes issued in February 2025 [D398][P1][P2].
Liquidity is $2,940.6 million of cash and investments against a 3.56x current ratio, the window low [D397][F180][D565].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% to 1,694.6 million [D401][D402][D425][X150].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last nine years, 191.1% of the operating loss [R2][D390][D404].
Net cash has fallen four years running into net debt, from $1,439.8 million in FY2021 to -$596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D211][D399].
Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 171.7% in FY2025 [R4][D307][D354][D402].
Operating margin: a move above the -9.0% FY2025 level would extend the narrowing trend, while a slip back toward the -32.4% median would reverse it [F30][D555].
Free-cash-flow margin: holding above the 7.4% FY2025 high would confirm the cash trend; falling below the -4.1% median would break it [D560][D561].
Net cash: a return above zero from -$596.3 million would reverse the four-year slide, which the FY2026 10-K will show [D399].
